segments: Tenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
Manuel the Patrician [rebelled] against Theophilus,
and came to al-Ma'mun,
and incited him to invade the territory of the Romans.
And in June al-Ma'mun entered,
and subdued four fortresses in Cappadocia.
And in Iyyar of the year 1142
[1142 of the Greeks], he entered again and encamped against the fortress of Lulon (Lulwah?),
and was not able to take it.
And after a year, when its inhabitants were pressed by hunger, they surrendered to 'Ujayf.
And Manuel the Patrician deserted the Arabs and returned to Theophilus.
Al-Ma'mun, then, was enraged and swore that he would invade and trample the Romans.
And when Theophilus heard, he was afraid,
and sent to al-Ma'mun regarding peace,
and offering to give tribute.
And he replied:
"On this condition will I make peace:
that you proclaim me your king;
and concerning the amount of the tribute,
whether it be great or small,
I will not contend."
Theophilus, however, when he heard these things, was silent,
and did not reply further.
And al-Ma'mun went to Cilicia,
and there came to him an impostor who said
that he was of the lineage of the kings.
And al-Ma'mun received him,
and commanded Job, the patriarch of the Chalcedonians, and he prayed over him,
and consecrated him king,
and bound a crown upon him.
And after he had been in the camp of the Arabs for two years,
and not one of the Romans came to him,
he apostatized to Islam at the hands of Abu Ishaq, the brother {OCR: 'son'} of al-Ma'mun.
And the bishops also gathered and excommunicated Job the patriarch, who had consecrated him.
And in the year 1143
[1143 of the Greeks,
832 of our Lord], al-Ma'mun went into Egypt,
and with him was Mor Dionysius the Patriarch.
And he found that the Nile had frozen,
a thing which had never been heard of before. And in the month of Iyyar, al-Ma'mun invaded the land of the Romans,
and with him were his two sons {OCR: brother and son}, al-Mu'tasim and al-'Abbas.
And he gathered artisans as if for the rebuilding of Tyana, which had been destroyed by the Arabs.
And there he fell sick and died on Wednesday,
the eighth of the seventh month, the year 218 [of the Arabs],
[having reigned eight years and eight months / Bedjan note: al-Mu'tasim his son {OCR?}].
When al-Ma'mun died,
there arose confusion among the Arabs for three days as to which of the two [contenders] should reign.
And while all of them were gathered,
suddenly the curtain of the door was lifted,
and al-'Abbas came out and said:
"The kingdom belongs to al-Mu'tasim
henceforth!"
notes: 218 of the Hagarenes [833 of our Lord]; and he was buried in Tarsus of Cilicia.
